subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Ultimatum Game
description: A quick, practical guide to The Ultimatum Game.

hook.text: You receive $100 to split with a stranger. You offer $1 and keep $99. The stranger rejects it, and you both get nothing.

buildup.text: In the ultimatum game, one player proposes a split and the other accepts or rejects. Rejection means both get zero.

discovery.text: Rational theory says accept any offer above zero. Experiments show offers below 20% are usually rejected.

twist.text: Offers vary by culture. The Machiguenga in Peru offer about 15%. American students offer about 45%.

climax.text: The ultimatum game proves humans are not pure profit maximizers. We punish unfairness even at personal cost.

punchline.text: We burn money to punish greed. Fairness is that powerful.

quiz.question: Why do people reject low offers in the ultimatum game?
options: They do not understand they will also get nothing
They prefer punishment of unfairness over personal profit
The game rules require rejection of low offers
